text:
maria: quick heads-up — I have a repro that shows KV cache memory climbing with >32k token contexts on Dedicated, but not consistently on Hosted or Private. sharing traces in a sec

kevin: curious — is it growth (leak) or fragmentation + paging?

maria: looks like fragmentation + paging/backpressure. we hit a steady-state where reclaim can't keep up; allocator stays fragmented and we see pagefault storming on some Dedicated pools

anika: do we have perf maps? can you paste the hot stacks?

maria: attaching short extract from perf script: `
    perf script: kv_cache_alloc+0x1a / serving::evict_page
    page_fault_handler+0x3f / mm
    reclaim_slab+0x12c
`

maria: also seeing repeating pattern: small allocs for KV frames, then a burst of full-page evicts => expensive memcpy loops

ryan: that smells like different kernel page size/hugepage config between envs. Dedicated hosts might not have transparent hugepages enabled, or userland pinned frames behave differently on our onprem drivers

kevin: any network/VPC differences? MTU or GSO offload could alter DMA chunking and cause different fragmentation?

anika: yep — on one Dedicated cluster MTU=9000, Hosted is 1500, Private onprem varies. we saw earlier that nvlink+large MTU made write bursts align with page boundaries more nicely, lowering fragmentation

maria: interesting — in the repro I toggled config: disabling continuous-batching reduces fragmentation (fewer small frames). enabling prefix caching increases reuse but also increases long-lived frames which then becomes sticky in slabs

perf-bot: trace snippet from the Dedicated repro run (timestamps relative):

    [100ms] kv_insert(seq=1540, size=6144)
    [140ms] kv_insert(seq=1541, size=512)
    [180ms] kv_evict(batch=128) -> memcpy loop 0.9ms/op
    [190ms] pagefault flood -> reclaim attempts 24/sec

maria: result summary: Dedicated shows sustained reclaim cycles, Hosted sometimes spikes but recovers, Private (onprem) depends on driver + cgroup memsw settings. config drift across the fleets probably explains differences

ryan: what about jemalloc vs system malloc flags? some Dedicated AMIs we rolled had jemalloc tunables changed (background_thread=false) which prevents async purging

kevin: we should check two things: 1) allocator purge/decay settings, 2) kernel vm.* tunables (vfs_cache_pressure, swappiness, dirty_writeback_centisecs) across nodes

anika: also add: batching heuristic. I instrumented the request inter-arrival histogram — when batching window is small we produce many small KV frames that scatter across pages. Increasing batching window from 2ms to 6ms collapsed small frames into fewer larger frames and lowered fragmentation by ~37% in the Hosted run

maria: plan proposal:
- capture config diffs (sysctl, jemalloc conf, MTU, NIC offloads, kernel version) across a sample of Dedicated/Hosted/Private hosts
- run controlled microbench with adjustable batching/incubation to see KV frame size distribution
- prototype a reclamation backoff that prefers coalescing small free slots instead of immediate page evict

kevin: +1. also add an experiment to temporarily cap KV cache entries per-tenant to test whether eviction pressure masks the problem

ryan: I'll open a small playbook to gather sysctl & ethtool settings across clusters. tagging infra leads.

maria: dropping a quick repro command for folks to run (Hosted-safe):

    ./kv_repro --mode=chat --tokens=40000 --batch-window-us=2000 --emit-trace > trace.log

anika: thanks — I'll run this on Private node with different driver builds and report back.

maria: one more note — logs show a fallback to model-variant when latency SLOs hit; that changes request shape and can make the fragging go away (we saw that in Hosted). keep an eye on rollouts as confounding factor

kevin: good catch. sounds like config drift + batching heuristic interactions + allocator/runtime tunables. actionable next steps look solid. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: created perf ticket INF-3258 with attached traces and heap profiles

maria: thanks all — i'll collect diffs and post a short matrix tomorrow. if anyone sees immediate wins (jemalloc async purge, bump batch-window) please shout here
